scope: Owner asks every animal be reconsidered assuming appearance is bad. No inherited technical or lenient visual pass constitutes appearance approval. Existing phone selections/Done/notes retained.
animation_policy: Existing animations accepted for now. Do not repair/rebake; future long pass ordered by owner, using AI video.

animals.name: Hare
animals.body_and_pattern_review: All coat and distinct attachment examples reviewed at prototype standard; secondary limitations in exact-SHA critic gate.

secondary_polish.issue: The eye corners show flat gray wedges and the exposed brown iris reads subdued next to the brighter amber actual profile reference.
The white muzzle/chin area is a fairly round, regular patch and the mouth is a tiny isolated mark; a less regular fur transition would look more natural at close inspection.

Fur detail is denser around the head and upper neck than on the body. A faint pale, smooth nape/shoulder transition is visible from behind; it is mild at full-body size rather than a dominant broken paint region.

animals.name: Rabbit
animals.body_and_pattern_review: All coat and distinct attachment examples reviewed at prototype standard; secondary limitations in exact-SHA critic gate.

secondary_polish.issue: The forehead-to-nose profile is somewhat straight and pointed, and the white muzzle is thin from the side compared with the fuller soft muzzle of the actual side photograph. This remains recognisable at prototype scale.
The pale gray eye-corner wedge and sharp lower outer lid angle can look synthetic in close views.
Head and neck fur detail is denser and more mottled than the body. The rear nape has a mild change in fur scale/brightness where it meets the shoulders; further blending would improve close viewing.

animals.name: Red fox
animals.body_and_pattern_review: All coat and distinct attachment examples reviewed at prototype standard; secondary limitations in exact-SHA critic gate.

secondary_polish.finding: Alternate-coat cheek boundaries and pale inner-ear patches are more abrupt than the red woodland coat. Dark cross, silver, pale and russet variants would benefit from a softer fur-edged pigment transition. This remains a secondary material issue at the supplied full-body scale.

Close-profile eye has a small exposed grey crescent and very regular vertical pupil. Slightly subtler rim integration would improve the close-up; paired position and general slit-pupil appearance are plausible.
Body fur has less detail than the painted head, particularly around the rear neck. The join is sufficiently blended for this prototype; matching texture frequency would improve polish.

animals.name: Wolf
animals.body_and_pattern_review: Remaining general body/pattern review not certified by this face pass.

animals.name: Wild goat
animals.body_and_pattern_review: All coat and distinct attachment examples reviewed at prototype standard; secondary limitations in exact-SHA critic gate.

secondary_polish.finding: Current beard has a connected filled upper tuft and taper, without the large open wire-like gaps. It is narrow and relatively straight in close profile but reads as a goat beard at full-body scale.
secondary_polish.action: Optional broader irregular clump contour and slight curvature would give a softer tuft; no longer a major attachment fault.

secondary_polish.finding: Lateral eye placement is plausible and narrowness from the front is expected. In both profiles the aperture reads as a narrow black capsule with very little gold iris and conspicuous pale lower edging. Reference profile has a fuller visible gold iris and softly integrated dark lid.
secondary_polish.action: Consider slightly fuller vertical aperture/visible gold iris and softer lower edging; preserve lateral placement and horizontal pupil.

secondary_polish.finding: Sharper photo-like head/upper-neck fur changes into much smoother body fur around the neck and withers, especially warm and pale coats.
secondary_polish.action: Soften the change of detail scale into the shoulder.

secondary_polish.finding: Uniform pale fine grid-like relief looks somewhat manufactured.
secondary_polish.action: Optional restrained tonal variation and less uniform growth relief; current material remains acceptable at prototype scale.

animals.name: Bison
animals.body_and_pattern_review: All coat and distinct attachment examples reviewed at prototype standard; secondary limitations in exact-SHA critic gate.

secondary_polish: The forehead and shoulder silhouette are smoother and more dome-like than the shaggy photographic examples; a little less uniform surface character would help at close range, but the hump, massive front half, compact muzzle, beard and short curved horns already identify a credible bison prototype.
At eye-audit scale the lower lip/nasal silhouette is angular and the eyes are small dark slits. These remain readable and reasonably integrated; refinement is secondary at this standard.

Coat03 is explicitly a colour-only shedding overlay study. Its soft, flat, somewhat rounded patches suggest pigment differences; they do not reproduce the dangling physical mats in the shedding photograph. No physical wool-clump success is claimed.

Coat05 broken brindle is deliberately hypothetical and rather faint. The hypothetical coats and smaller horn studies are visually coherent options, not validation of a particular real population, sex-specific body or calf morphology.

animals.name: Native detritivorous flies (guild)
animals.body_and_pattern_review: All coat and distinct attachment examples reviewed at prototype standard; secondary limitations in exact-SHA critic gate.

secondary_polish: Eyes are small faceted buttons compared with the broader, oval compound-eye masses in the supplied photos. This is visible in front and oblique stills but does not obscure the tiny flying-insect read; enlarge/elongate the eye masses only if close presentation becomes part of the intended use.

Thorax and abdomen are smooth simple lobes, and the six legs are sparse angular lines. Surface segmentation, bristles, tarsal detail and the more domed reference thorax are omitted; acceptable simplification for this tiny ambient proxy.

Green and blue coats communicate the metallic bottle-fly color families through glossy pigment, though the uniform color and black eyes are less varied than the actual references. Brown, black and muted bronze retain clear silhouette contrast.

independent_baseline_review.scope: Canonical earlier baseline, not acceptance of newer anatomy work.

animals.name: Reindeer
animals.body_and_pattern_review: All coat and distinct attachment examples reviewed at prototype standard; secondary limitations in exact-SHA critic gate.

secondary_polish: In the close profile renders, the upper edge of the lower antler web has a short straight shelf and the web is more modest than the broad palm visible in the profile photograph. Softening that edge and adding restrained irregular breadth could improve species specificity, but its current silhouette remains plausible and continuous.
Close head renders show softer nose/nostril paint and more obvious thin whisker lines than the reference. Better nostril definition and subtler whiskers would improve close-up finish.

Head/upper-neck fur is higher contrast and more directional than the simpler body coat, particularly in Brown summer. The full-body transition is readable and acceptable, but more consistent fur scale would polish it.
The eye highlight/iris detail is very subdued in profile and the lids can read slightly heavy at close range; this does not create an obvious placement or integration failure.

animals.name: Moose
animals.body_and_pattern_review: All coat and distinct attachment examples reviewed at prototype standard; secondary limitations in exact-SHA critic gate.

secondary_polish.issue: Antler palms are very flat, pale and angular, with fairly regular sharp triangular tines and visible faceted palm shading. More cupping, varied tine lengths/curvature and restrained bone variation would improve comparison with the actual NPS/FWS antlers. Current forms retain the essential moose palm-and-tine silhouette.

Near-root upward tines overlap the ears strongly in close profiles, forming a cone-like shape in front of each ear. No detached join is established by these images, but clearer clearance and less overlap would make the crown easier to read.
The pale muzzle whisker fan is conspicuous and more visible on one side in the frontal render; reduce its brightness/regularity or verify paired placement for a less wire-like appearance.

Head and upper-neck paint has higher contrast and coarser apparent fur detail than the smoother body. The texture-frequency transition is visible, especially behind the ears and upper shoulder, but no hard rectangular cutoff is apparent in full-body views.

Black-brown coat has stronger pale facial mottling than the ordinary dark moose photos. Softer mottling would look more natural, while the explicitly hypothetical coat can retain its stronger variation.

animals.name: Raccoon
animals.body_and_pattern_review: All coat and distinct attachment examples reviewed at prototype standard; secondary limitations in exact-SHA critic gate.

secondary_polish.finding: Eyes are very glossy and nearly uniformly black, with limited visible lid structure. They look slightly bead-like in close-up. A subtler highlight and more evident narrow upper lid would improve realism; placement and dark round-eye appearance remain plausible.

Detailed brownish head/nape fur changes to simpler grey-brown body fur behind the ears. The small brown nape patch and texture-frequency shift are noticeable in rear/side inspection; soften this transition for polish. It does not form a dominant complete collar or obscure the silhouette.
Tail rings are unusually clean and uniform. Mild edge variation would make the pattern less graphic while retaining clear recognition.
